cim: Students face new AI rules at Central Florida schools
cim_eredeti: Students face new AI rules at Central Florida schools
szoveg_eredeti:
ORLANDO, Fla. — Artificial intelligence is transforming how students study, write and complete school assignments.

In response to the evolving technology, Orange County Public Schools implemented a new policy for the current academic year.

Under the policy, students must obtain permission from an instructor before using artificial intelligence and are restricted strictly to district-sanctioned platforms.

These district limitations do not apply to students after they exit the school environment.

Consequently, guardians are urged to ask their children to explain their homework assignments to ensure they grasp the subject matter and reach their conclusions without outside assistance.

Maya Israel helped create the Florida AI Education Task Force, which aims to formulate guidelines for classroom implementation.

According to Israel, studies have not yet established whether artificial intelligence impacts a student’s critical thinking skills or interpersonal connections.

Despite the uncertainty, area students have identified benefits, including a high school student aiming to study university neuroscience who uses AI to help comprehend brain function and neurological therapies.
